quantx_engine.threshold_curve(distances=None, p_phys_range=(0.005, 0.2), n_points=15, n_shots=500, n_rounds=1, decoder='mwpm', seed=None)[source]¶

Sweep p_phys for multiple distances and estimate the threshold.

For each (d, p_phys) pair, a FTQCPipeline is constructed and n_shots trials are run. The threshold is estimated as the average of pairwise crossing points between adjacent distance curves (see threshold_crossing()).

Parameters:

  • distances (list[int] | None) – Code distances to sweep. Defaults to [3, 5, 7].

  • p_phys_range ((float, float)) – (p_min, p_max) interval for the sweep.

  • n_points (int) – Number of evenly-spaced points in p_phys_range.

  • n_shots (int) – Monte Carlo shots per (d, p_phys) point.

  • n_rounds (int) – Syndrome extraction rounds per trial.

  • decoder ({"mwpm", "greedy"})

  • seed (int | None)

Return type:

ThresholdCurveResult

quantx_engine.threshold_crossing(result)[source]¶

Re-estimate the threshold crossing from a ThresholdCurveResult.

Uses pairwise linear interpolation between consecutive distance curves to find the p_phys value where larger distance transitions from worse (above threshold) to better (below threshold).

Returns None if no crossing is detectable.

class quantx_engine.FTQCResourceEstimator(target_logical_error_rate, physical_error_rate, threshold=0.01, prefactor=0.1, max_distance=51)[source]¶

Bases: object

Estimate physical qubit and magic-state resources for fault-tolerant QC.

Uses the surface code threshold model from Fowler et al. (2012). The logical error rate per round scales as

p_L ≈ A × (p_phys / p_th)^{⌊(d+1)/2⌋}

where A ≈ 0.1, p_th ≈ 0.01 (1% threshold for the depolarizing model).

References

[Fowler2012]

Fowler, A. G. et al. (2012). Surface codes: Towards practical large-scale quantum computation. Phys. Rev. A 86, 032324. https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.86.032324

Parameters:

  • target_logical_error_rate (float) – Desired logical error rate per logical gate.

  • physical_error_rate (float) – Physical qubit error rate (must be < threshold ≈ 0.01).

  • threshold (float, default 0.01) – Surface code threshold (default: 1%).

  • prefactor (float, default 0.1) – Pre-exponential constant A in p_L = A * (p/p_th)^t.

  • max_distance (int, default 51) – Maximum code distance to search.

Examples

>>> est = FTQCResourceEstimator(target_logical_error_rate=1e-10,
...                             physical_error_rate=1e-3)
>>> result = est.estimate()
>>> print(result)
ResourceEstimate(d=7, p_phys=1.00e-03, p_target=1.00e-10, qubits=98, p_logical=...)
__init__(target_logical_error_rate, physical_error_rate, threshold=0.01, prefactor=0.1, max_distance=51)[source]¶

class quantx_engine.ExcitedStateVQE(hamiltonian, n_states=3, method='exact', penalty_weight=10.0)[source]¶

Bases: object

Variational computation of multiple excited states.

Parameters:

  • hamiltonian (PauliHamiltonian) – The molecular Hamiltonian (or any Hermitian operator).

  • n_states (int, default 3) – Number of states to compute (including the ground state).

  • method ({"exact", "deflation", "folded_spectrum"}, default "exact") –

    Algorithm to use:

    • "exact" — full numpy diagonalisation (best for n ≤ 16).

    • "deflation" — variational deflation: penalise previously found states with a positive-definite projection term.

    • "folded_spectrum" — minimise ⟨(H−ω)²⟩ for a sequence of ω values spaced across the spectrum.

  • penalty_weight (float, default 10.0) – Weight λ used in the deflation penalty ΔH = λ Σ |ψ_k⟩⟨ψ_k|. Only used when method="deflation".

class quantx_engine.KibbleZurekScaling(n_sites, J=1.0, n_steps=50, *, model=None)[source]¶

Bases: object

Kibble-Zurek scaling across the 1D transverse-field Ising critical point.

Linearly ramps the transverse field h from h_i > h_c to h_f < h_c (quenching through the critical point h_c = 1) at rate v = (h_i − h_f)/T, then measures the density of domain walls (defects) created.

Parameters:

  • n_sites (int) – Number of sites (qubits) in the 1D chain.

  • J (float, default 1.0) – Ising coupling strength.

  • n_steps (int, default 50) – Number of discrete Trotter steps for the quench.

class quantx_engine.CVaRQAOA(cost_diagonal=None, n_qubits=None, n_layers=1, alpha=0.25, exact_optimum=None, *, problem=None, p=None, seed=None)[source]¶

Bases: object

QAOA with Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) objective.

Replaces the standard expectation-value objective ⟨H_C⟩ with CVaR_α = E[C(x) | C(x) ≤ VaR_α], which focuses training on the best-α fraction of measurement outcomes.

Parameters:

  • cost_diagonal (np.ndarray, shape (2**n,)) – Pre-computed cost C(x) for every computational basis state.

  • n_qubits (int)

  • n_layers (int, default 1) – QAOA depth p.

  • alpha (float, default 0.25) – CVaR confidence level ∈ (0, 1]. alpha=1 recovers standard QAOA.

  • exact_optimum (float | None) – Known exact optimum for computing approximation ratio.

    Initialisation strategy:

    • "fixed" — γ_k = 0.1k/p, β_k = π/4 (1 − k/p).

class quantx_engine.CatNoiseModel(kappa_1=0.01, kappa_phi=0.001, alpha_sq=4.0)[source]¶

Bases: object

Noise model for a Kerr-cat qubit.

Variables:

  • kappa_1 (float) – Single-photon loss rate (κ₁). Sets the overall photon-loss timescale.

  • kappa_phi (float) – Pure dephasing rate (κ_φ) in the oscillator frame.

  • alpha_sq (float) – Cat-state amplitude squared |α|². Controls the biased-noise ratio.

Notes

The bit-flip rate scales as exp(−2|α|²·κ₁/κ₂) and the phase-flip rate scales as |α|²·(κ₁ + κ_φ) (linear in cat size).

kappa_1: float = 0.01¶
kappa_phi: float = 0.001¶
alpha_sq: float = 4.0¶
property bit_flip_rate: float¶

Logical X error rate ~ exp(−2|α|²)·κ₁ (exponentially suppressed).

property phase_flip_rate: float¶

Logical Z error rate ~ |α|²·(κ₁ + κ_φ) (linear in cat size).

property bias_ratio: float¶

η = phase_flip_rate / bit_flip_rate (should be ≫ 1 for a useful cat).

class quantx_engine.CatQubit(K=1.0, eps2=4.0, N_max=30, noise=None, *, alpha=None, kerr=None, truncation=None)[source]¶

Bases: object

Kerr-cat qubit in a truncated Fock space.

The Kerr-cat Hamiltonian is

H = −K a†²a² + ε₂(a†² + a²)

which stabilises a two-component cat state with amplitude α = √(ε₂/K).

Parameters:

  • K (float) – Kerr nonlinearity (anharmonicity). Must be > 0.

  • eps2 (float) – Two-photon drive amplitude. Must be > 0.

  • N_max (int) – Fock-space truncation. Should satisfy N_max ≫ 2|α|² + 10.

  • noise (CatNoiseModel | None) – Optional noise model. If None, uses CatNoiseModel defaults with alpha_sq derived from eps2/K.

__init__(K=1.0, eps2=4.0, N_max=30, noise=None, *, alpha=None, kerr=None, truncation=None)[source]¶

Logical |0_L⟩ = normalised even cat state |C_α+⟩.

encode_1()[source]¶

Logical |1_L⟩ = normalised odd cat state |C_α−⟩.

property logical_z: ndarray¶

Z_L = exp(iπ n̂) (photon-number parity).

Type:

Logical Z operator

property logical_x: ndarray¶

swaps |C_α+⟩ ↔ |C_α−⟩ within the code subspace.

Constructs the unitary X_L = |1_L⟩⟨0_L| + |0_L⟩⟨1_L| + (I − P_code), which acts as Pauli X on the {|0_L⟩, |1_L⟩} code subspace and as the identity on its orthogonal complement. This is exact for any α.

Type:

Logical X operator

class quantx_engine.GKPState(delta=0.3, N_max=60, *, truncation=None)[source]¶

Bases: object

Finite-energy GKP (Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill) code state.

The ideal GKP code encodes a qubit in a harmonic oscillator with stabilisers S_q = e^{i2√π q̂} and S_p = e^{-i2√π p̂}. The finite-energy approximation uses a Gaussian envelope with width δ in Fock space.

Parameters:

  • delta (float) – Envelope/squeezing parameter δ > 0. Smaller δ → better code words but more photons. Physical squeezing in dB ≈ −20 log₁₀(δ/√(2π)).

  • N_max (int) – Fock-space truncation.

Notes

The code words are constructed as a superposition of displaced squeezed vacuum states at lattice points n√π in phase space.

class quantx_engine.GKPDecoder(gkp, n_rounds=1)[source]¶

Bases: object

Small-Big-Small (SBS) shift error correction for GKP codes.

The SBS sequence applies alternating small and big displacements to map shift errors back toward the lattice points:

D_small(−ξ) · D_big(+ξ + correction) · D_small(−ξ)

where the correction direction is estimated from a syndrome measurement of the shift-error magnitude.

Parameters:

  • gkp (GKPState) – The GKP state object (defines δ, N_max, lattice).

  • n_rounds (int) – Number of SBS correction rounds to apply.

class quantx_engine.MagicStateFactory(protocol='7_to_1', input_error_rate=0.01)[source]¶

Bases: object

Simulates magic state distillation for fault-tolerant T gates.

Two protocols are supported:

  • 7-to-1 — consumes 7 noisy |T⟩ copies; uses the [[7,1,3]] Steane code to detect and discard corrupted states. Output error rate ≈ 35 ε³.

  • 15-to-1 — consumes 15 noisy copies; uses the [[15,1,3]] Reed-Muller code. Output error rate ≈ 35 ε³ (with a smaller coefficient in practice).

Parameters:

  • protocol ({"7_to_1", "15_to_1"}) – Distillation protocol.

  • input_error_rate (float) – Per-copy error rate of the noisy input |T⟩ states (must be in (0, 1)).

class quantx_engine.FTTGate(magic_state_fidelity=0.999999)[source]¶

Bases: object

Fault-tolerant T gate via magic state injection (gate teleportation).

Protocol¶

  1. Prepare ancilla in |T⟩ = (|0⟩ + e^{iπ/4}|1⟩)/√2.

  2. Apply CNOT (data qubit = control, ancilla = target).

  3. Measure ancilla in the Z basis.

  4. If outcome is |1⟩, apply S correction to the data qubit.

The resulting operation applies T to the data qubit (up to global phase).

Fidelity of the injected |T⟩ magic state with the ideal state. Controls the effective gate error rate.

class quantx_engine.OOVQESolver(h_core, n_orb, n_circuit_params=2, energy_fn=None, max_iterations=30, inner_steps=20, lr_circuit=0.05, lr_orbital=0.02, conv_tol=1e-05, eps=0.0001)[source]¶

Bases: object

Orbital-optimised VQE solver.

Uses an alternating minimisation strategy:

  1. Inner VQE: minimise ⟨ψ(θ)|H(κ)|ψ(θ)⟩ over circuit parameters θ by gradient descent.

  2. Orbital gradient step: update orbital parameters κ by one step of gradient descent on the orbital rotation manifold.

Parameters:

  • h_core (array-like, shape (n_orb, n_orb)) – One-electron integrals (core Hamiltonian) in the initial MO basis.

  • n_orb (int) – Number of spatial orbitals.

  • n_circuit_params (int) – Number of parametric circuit (ansatz) angles.

  • energy_fn (callable or None) – energy_fn(h_rotated, theta) -> float computing the VQE energy for given rotated one-electron integrals and circuit parameters. If None, the built-in 2-orbital JW model is used.

  • max_iterations (int) – Maximum number of macro (OO) iterations.

  • inner_steps (int) – Number of circuit gradient steps per macro iteration.

  • lr_circuit (float) – Learning rate for circuit parameter updates.

  • lr_orbital (float) – Learning rate for orbital rotation parameter updates.

  • conv_tol (float) – Convergence threshold: |ΔE| < conv_tol terminates the loop.

  • eps (float) – Finite-difference step for gradient estimates.

class quantx_engine.QSPAnglesFinder(degree, n_grid=200, *, target=None)[source]¶

Bases: object

Compute QSP phase angles for standard polynomial targets.

QSP realises the top-left element of the QSP unitary

[U_QSP]₀₀ = P(x)

where P is a polynomial of degree d with |P(x)| ≤ 1 for x ∈ [-1, 1] and the parity of d matches the parity of the number of signal queries.

This class provides analytic angle sequences for common targets (where closed-form formulas are known) and a gradient-descent solver for arbitrary polynomials.

Parameters:

  • degree (int) – Target polynomial degree.

  • n_grid (int) – Number of grid points used for error estimation.

__init__(degree, n_grid=200, *, target=None)[source]¶
run()[source]¶

Compute phase angles for the configured target polynomial.

Dispatches based on the target kwarg passed to __init__: - "chebyshev" → chebyshev() with k = degree - "sign" → sign_function() - "threshold" → threshold() - None → chebyshev() (default)

chebyshev(k)[source]¶

Return phase angles that realise the Chebyshev polynomial T_k(x).

T_k(cos θ) = cos(kθ), so P(x) = Re[e^{ik·arccos x}].

The QSP angles are φⱼ = 0 for j = 1, …, d-1 and φ₀ = φ_d = π/4, scaled to match the Chebyshev target (analytic construction for even d).

Parameters:

k (int) – Chebyshev order (must equal self.degree).

sign_function(delta=0.1, scale=0.9)[source]¶

Return phase angles approximating sign(x) with error δ outside [-δ, δ].

Uses a degree-d odd polynomial approximation of the step function. The phases are found via a minimax gradient-descent fit.

Parameters:

  • delta (float) – Half-width of the transition region.

  • scale (float) – Target value: P(x) ≈ ±scale for |x| > delta.

hamiltonian_simulation(t, order=None)[source]¶

Phase angles for Hamiltonian simulation e^{-iHt} to a given order.

Realises the polynomial P(x) = Σ_{k=0}^{d/2} (-it)^k x^k / k! (truncated Taylor series of e^{-ixt}, rescaled for x ∈ [-1, 1]).

Parameters:

  • t (float) – Evolution time.

  • order (int or None) – Truncation order; defaults to self.degree.

threshold(threshold_x=0.0)[source]¶

Phase angles for a step function at threshold_x.

Approximates P(x) ≈ 0 for x < threshold_x and ≈ 1 for x > threshold_x. (Odd-degree polynomial approximation.)

class quantx_engine.QSVTCircuit(phases, block_encoding, n_signal, alpha=1.0)[source]¶

Bases: object

Build and simulate a QSVT circuit given phase angles and a block-encoding.

QSVT applies a polynomial transformation P(σᵢ) to the singular values σᵢ of an operator A, where A is embedded as the top-left block of a unitary block-encoding U_A:

⟨G|U_A|G⟩ = A / α (‖A‖ ≤ α)

The QSVT circuit interleaves queries to U_A (and U_A†) with single-qubit Z-rotation projectors controlled on the block flag qubit:

U_QSVT = Π̃_{φ₀} ∏_{k=1}^{d} [ U_A · Π_{φₖ} ] (even d)

where Π_φ = e^{iφ|0⟩⟨0|} ⊗ I_A is a reflection through the signal subspace.

Parameters:

  • phases (array-like, shape (d+1,)) – QSP phase angles Φ.

  • block_encoding (array-like or callable) – Either a 2m × 2m unitary U_A (dense matrix) or a callable U_A(state) → state for larger spaces.

  • n_signal (int) – Dimension of the signal (block) subspace (= n_qubits of A).

  • alpha (float) – Block-encoding normalisation factor (‖A‖ ≤ alpha).

__init__(phases, block_encoding, n_signal, alpha=1.0)[source]¶

This is a simplified simulation that applies the QSP scalar circuit to each singular value σᵢ of the operator A embedded in the block-encoding, effectively computing Σᵢ P(σᵢ/α)|uᵢ⟩⟨vᵢ| @ state.

Parameters:

state (array-like, shape (n,) where n = 2^n_signal) – Input state vector in the signal subspace.

Returns:

Output state after the polynomial transformation.

ndarray, shape (n,)

class quantx_engine.McLachlanSolver(ansatz, hamiltonian, n_params, dt=0.01, evolution='real', integrator='euler', reg=1e-06, eps=1e-05)[source]¶

Bases: object

Time-evolve a parametrised ansatz under the McLachlan variational principle.

Parameters:

  • ansatz (callable) – Function ansatz(params) -> state_vector that maps variational parameters to the corresponding normalised quantum state.

  • hamiltonian (array-like or callable) – Hamiltonian. Either a 2-D complex array (dense matrix) or a callable H(state) -> ndarray representing the action H|ψ⟩.

  • n_params (int) – Number of variational parameters.

  • dt (float) – Time step.

  • evolution ({"real", "imaginary"}) – “real”: unitary Schrödinger evolution under e^{-iHt}. “imaginary”: non-unitary cooling under e^{-Ht} (find ground state).

  • integrator ({"euler", "rk4"}) – ODE integrator.

  • reg (float) – Regularisation added to the diagonal of the metric tensor M to avoid singular linear systems.

  • eps (float) – Finite-difference step for computing parameter gradients ∂|ψ⟩/∂θᵢ.

__init__(ansatz, hamiltonian, n_params, dt=0.01, evolution='real', integrator='euler', reg=1e-06, eps=1e-05)[source]¶

class quantx_engine.HypergraphProductCode(code1, code2)[source]¶

Bases: object

CSS quantum code via the hypergraph product of two classical codes.

Given classical codes C₁ = [n₁, k₁] with parity-check H₁ (m₁×n₁) and C₂ = [n₂, k₂] with H₂ (m₂×n₂), the hypergraph product code has

  • Physical qubits: N = n₁n₂ + m₁m₂

  • Logical qubits: K = k₁k₂ + k₁’k₂’ (k_i’ = n_i − m_i if H_i is full rank)

  • X stabilisers: Hx = [H₁ ⊗ I_{n₂} | I_{m₁} ⊗ H₂ᵀ]

  • Z stabilisers: Hz = [I_{n₁} ⊗ H₂ | H₁ᵀ ⊗ I_{m₂}]

Parameters:

  • code1 (ClassicalCode) – First classical seed code C₁.

  • code2 (ClassicalCode) – Second classical seed code C₂.

__init__(code1, code2)[source]¶
property Hx: ndarray¶

X-stabiliser matrix (binary).

property Hz: ndarray¶

Z-stabiliser matrix (binary).

property n_qubits: int¶

Total number of physical qubits.

property n: int¶

Alias for n_qubits.

property n_x_checks: int¶

Number of X parity checks (rows of Hx).

property n_z_checks: int¶

Number of Z parity checks (rows of Hz).

property k: int¶

Number of logical qubits K = n − rank(Hx) − rank(Hz).

Uses the CSS formula which correctly accounts for both stabiliser sectors of the hypergraph product, including the transpose-sector logicals that the simple k₁k₂ product formula misses.

property n_x_stabs: int¶

Alias for n_x_checks.

property n_z_stabs: int¶

Alias for n_z_checks.

Bases: object

Belief-propagation decoder for binary LDPC codes.

Implements flooding-schedule BP over the Tanner graph with optional ordered-statistics decoding (OSD) post-processing when BP fails to converge.

  • max_iter (int) – Maximum number of BP iterations.

  • osd_order (int) – Order of OSD post-processing (0 = no OSD; 1 = test all single-bit flips on the unreliable positions).

Decode a syndrome to an error estimate.

Parameters:

  • channel_llr (array-like, shape (n,) or None) – Log-likelihood ratios log(P(e=0)/P(e=1)) for each bit. If None, a BSC model with error_rate is assumed for all bits.

  • error_rate (float) – BSC error probability used when channel_llr is None.

Returns:

  • converged (bool) – True if BP converged (zero residual syndrome), False otherwise.

Return type:

tuple[ndarray, bool]

quantx_engine.bicycle_code(L, a_shifts, b_shifts)[source]¶

Construct a quasi-cyclic bicycle (QC-LDPC) CSS code.

A bicycle code is built from two circulant matrices A, B of size L × L, where A = Σᵢ P^{aᵢ} and B = Σⱼ P^{bⱼ} (P is the L × L cyclic shift). The parity-check matrices are:

Hx = [A | B]      Hz = [Bᵀ | Aᵀ]

which are the hypergraph product of the circulant codes defined by A and B.

Parameters:

  • L (int) – Circulant size (must be > 0).

  • a_shifts (sequence of int) – Positions of the 1s in the first row of A (shifts of P).

  • b_shifts (sequence of int) – Positions of the 1s in the first row of B (shifts of P).

Returns:

The resulting bicycle CSS code.

Return type:

HypergraphProductCode

quantx_engine.backend_info()[source]¶

Return a capability summary for the active QuantX backend.

Checks whether the native C++ shared library is loaded (requires QUANTX_LIB_PATH to point to a compiled libquantx.so / quantx.dll), and returns a dict describing available features.

Returns:

Keys:

nativebool

True when the native C++ engine is available and loaded.

gpubool

True when the native engine was built with CUDA/OpenCL support.

versionstr

Version string (native engine version when available, else "pure-python-<__version__>").

solverslist[str]

Named physics solvers exposed by the native library (empty for pure-Python mode).

max_qubitsint | None

Practical qubit limit reported by the native circuit backend, or None in pure-Python mode.

Return type:

dict

Examples

>>> from quantx_engine import backend_info
>>> info = backend_info()
>>> info["native"]
False  # unless QUANTX_LIB_PATH is set and the library is compiled

class quantx_engine.Symbol(name)[source]¶

Bases: object

Named symbolic parameter for parametric gates (e.g. in VQE).

Use a Symbol wherever a rotation angle is expected. Before calling QuantumCircuit.run() you must bind all symbols to numeric values via the params argument:

theta = Symbol("theta")
qc    = QuantumCircuit(1)
qc.rx(theta, 0)
result = qc.run(n_shots=0, params={"theta": math.pi / 2})
Parameters:

name (str) – Human-readable name used as the key in the params dict.
